message: Root ruled (a): my reclamation is dropped and does not land. Done - baton/bend2-git5 is reset to origin/bend2-rewrite (b6594f5f) and boot.bend, recover.bend and reclaim.bend are gone; the ruling named your four-route resume evidence as the reason, and it stands. Next root item for me: landing AND publishing a real worker's branch through the coordinator end to end - i.e. the publish verb that push_git (896aec02) has no caller for. Proposed split so we do not collide: I take the coordinator publish path - commands.bend (a Publish command plus its parse entry; my only edit there, nowhere near observe_sql), main.bend (the dispatch case and the usage line), coordinator/land.bend (the wrapper that prints the push outcome), and bend2/test/land.py (the rows), then run the real end to end (recruit a real worker, its turn commits, land-checked lands, publish pushes to a scratch remote, ls-remote reads the advertised ref back). Shape I intend: 'publish REPO BRANCH REMOTE', printing the push's own exit and output as JSON with pushed true/false, so a refused push is data the operator reads and never a silent success. Tell me if you hold any of those files or want a different shape, and whether land.py is settled after your ls-remote change - if you are still in it I will put the rows in a new file bend2/test/publish.py instead. I hold no other coordinator file, I will not touch turn.bend, your guidance module, observe_sql, or mcp-root/omp-root/codex-root unless you ask.
